additional_prohibitions: Holders of federal and statewide public office.
Paid campaign staffers on Presidential campaigns.
Anyone working in a vote-tallying capacity, or who has the potential ability to observe official vote counts before they are public.
Third-party vendors and contractors (and employees thereof) of Presidential campaigns.
Paid employees of Democratic and Republican Party organizations, such as the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee or the Republican National Committee.
Paid employees of Political Action Committees (PACs) and “Super PACs” (independent expenditure only political committees).

Paid employees of major polling organizations. This prohibition does not apply to all employees of an organization that contains a polling division (e.g. the prohibition does not apply to all employees of Quinnipiac University despite the presence of Quinnipiac University’s polling division). The Exchange shall determine which polling organizations constitute “major” and may modify that determination at any time, and will post publicly a list of those organizations on its website

Employees of Decision Desks at major media organizations (including, but not necessarily exclusive to, Fox News, ABC News, AP, CNN, CBS News, Decision Desk HQ and NBC News). The Exchange shall determine which media organizations constitute “major” and may modify that determination at any time, and will post publicly a list of those organizations on its website.
All Electors who may cast ballots in connection with the determination of the President and/or Vice-President of the United States
All staff of the U.S. House of Representatives and its members
All staff of the U.S. Senate and its members.
All staff of the Office of the President of the United States
All staff of the Office of the Vice President of the United States
All staff of the U.S. Supreme Court and its Justices
Persons who are employed by any of the Source Agencies are not permitted to trade on the Contract.
Persons who hold any material, non-public information on the Underlying are not permitted to trade on the Contract.
Any candidate currently listed as a market within this event

normalized_rules.description:
The 2028 US Presidential Election is scheduled to take place on November 7, 2028.

This market will resolve to the person who wins the 2028 US Presidential Election.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race for the same candidate by the inauguration date (January 20, 2029) this market will resolve based on who is inaugurated.

eventMetadata.context_description: JD Vance holds the market lead at 25.3% as sitting vice president and early Republican frontrunner, backed by consistent primary polling advantages and alignment with the current administration’s base. Marco Rubio at 10.5% has narrowed gaps in recent surveys through stronger general-election matchups and cabinet visibility, while Democratic contenders including Jon Ossoff at 11.5%, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 10.3%, and Gavin Newsom at 8.5% reflect fragmented opposition support ahead of 2026 midterms. The wide field leaves room for consolidation around proven fundraisers, swing-state appeal, or late endorsements, with trader prices tracking name recognition and headline positioning more than settled nominations.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2026 MLB World Series. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2026 MLB World Series per the rules of MLB (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 MLB season is cancelled, postponed after December 31, 2026 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from MLB (https://www.mlb.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Los Angeles Dodgers hold the top implied probability at 31% thanks to their deep roster, strong NL West standing near 81-54, and historical postseason experience despite pitching uncertainties around Shohei Ohtani. The Milwaukee Brewers sit at 12% on the strength of the majors' best record (84-51) and dominant NL Central form. The New York Yankees (9.5%) and Tampa Bay Rays (7%) benefit from AL East contention, with the Rays at 80-54. Other contenders like the Atlanta Braves, Philadelphia Phillies, and Chicago Cubs reflect solid division or wild-card positioning and recent momentum, while lower probabilities for teams such as the Houston Astros and San Diego Padres align with middling records and tougher paths through expanded playoffs. Late-August injury reports and divisional races continue to shape trader consensus.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Republican Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Republican Party sources.

Any replacement of the Republican nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The tight contest between Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and J.D. Vance at near-even odds reflects trader assessments of their distinct bases within the Republican coalition ahead of the 2028 nomination. Vance benefits from his current role and alignment with core party priorities on trade, immigration enforcement, and institutional reform, while Kennedy draws support through crossover appeal on regulatory and health policy issues. Recent national and early-state polling shows both candidates maintaining steady but non-dominant shares among likely primary voters, with limited movement from endorsements or congressional actions. Rubio trails as a more conventional alternative, and the broader field remains fragmented. Key upcoming catalysts include midterm election results, confirmation votes, and any shifts in candidate positioning on foreign policy or fiscal matters that could consolidate support or prompt withdrawals.

resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Republican Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Republican Party sources.

Any replacement of the Republican nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

normalized_rules.description:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gadi Eisenkot leads trader expectations for Israel's next prime minister following the October 27, 2026 Knesset election, reflecting his Yashar party's consistent polling gains over Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud amid voter fatigue with the incumbent's security record after the October 2023 Hamas attack and subsequent conflicts. Recent surveys show Eisenkot's party often edging or tying Likud in projected seats while he leads as preferred prime minister, aided by his former IDF chief of staff background and broad appeal across centrist and right-leaning voters. Netanyahu retains core support but contends with coalition bloc shortfalls below 61 seats in most forecasts, prompting discussions of potential unity arrangements. Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman trail as secondary options in fragmented opposition scenarios. These dynamics align with current market pricing as traders weigh coalition formation prospects in Israel's proportional representation system.

Employees of exit-polling and election-night survey operations engaged by media organizations or campaigns in any race listed within this event, including but not limited to Edison Research and the National Election Pool.
series.title: House winner

resolution_criteria:
If the Republican Party has won control of the House in 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
This market may be determined early based on a consensus of media calls projecting control of the U.S. House. See full rules for details. Otherwise, victory will be determined by the party identification of the Speaker of the House on February 1, 2027.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Democratic polling leads on the generic congressional ballot, averaging around D+6 in recent surveys, combined with President Trump's approval rating near 38%, form the core driver behind trader consensus heavily favoring Democratic House control in 2026. This environment aligns with historical midterm patterns where the president's party often faces headwinds, and recent race rating updates from forecasters have shifted additional Republican-held districts toward Democrats. Mid-decade redistricting provided some structural gains for Republicans in targeted states, yet forecasts project Democratic seat gains sufficient for a majority in most simulations. With roughly two months until Election Day, these fundamentals continue to shape assessments of the narrow current GOP majority.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve to the player who wins the 2026 National League Cy Young Award.

In the event of a tie, this market will resolve according to the official winner as determined by MLB rules. If multiple winners are announced then this market will resolve to the player whose listed last name comes first alphabetically.

If the 2026 MLB season is cancelled, postponed after December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Major League Baseball; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Jacob Misiorowski's historic 2026 campaign as the Milwaukee Brewers' ace has driven overwhelming trader consensus around his NL Cy Young candidacy. Through 25 starts, the 24-year-old right-hander holds a 14-5 record with a 1.73 ERA, MLB-leading 222 strikeouts, and 0.75 WHIP over 151 innings, including an extended streak of quality starts and consistent triple-digit velocity. These numbers place him well ahead of established arms like Chris Sale and Cristopher Sanchez in traditional and advanced metrics. The Brewers' strong NL Central standing adds context to his workload and team success. A late-season injury, sharp decline in command, or voter emphasis on innings totals could still open a path for challengers.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2027 NFL league championship. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2027 NFL league championship per the rules of the NFL (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2027 NFL league championship game is cancelled, postponed after March 31, 2027 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from NFL (https://www.nfl.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Los Angeles Rams hold the clearest edge in the 2027 champion market after aggressive offseason additions, including the acquisition of reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and cornerback Trent McDuffie, built on a roster that reached the NFC Championship last season behind Matthew Stafford’s MVP campaign and weapons like Puka Nacua. This positions them ahead of a tightly bunched group where the Buffalo Bills, defending champion Seattle Seahawks, Baltimore Ravens, and others sit between roughly 4% and 9%. The compressed probabilities reflect broad NFL parity, with multiple clubs featuring established quarterbacks, recent playoff experience, and solid depth, while roster turnover for the Seahawks and the absence of any overwhelming favorite keep outcomes competitive heading into the 2026 season.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Republican Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Republican Party sources.

Any replacement of the Republican nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The tight contest between Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and J.D. Vance at near-even odds reflects trader assessments of their distinct bases within the Republican coalition ahead of the 2028 nomination. Vance benefits from his current role and alignment with core party priorities on trade, immigration enforcement, and institutional reform, while Kennedy draws support through crossover appeal on regulatory and health policy issues. Recent national and early-state polling shows both candidates maintaining steady but non-dominant shares among likely primary voters, with limited movement from endorsements or congressional actions. Rubio trails as a more conventional alternative, and the broader field remains fragmented. Key upcoming catalysts include midterm election results, confirmation votes, and any shifts in candidate positioning on foreign policy or fiscal matters that could consolidate support or prompt withdrawals.

normalized_rules.description:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Lula leads the 2026 Brazilian presidential race with a modest edge in trader consensus, reflecting his position as incumbent seeking a fourth term against a fragmented opposition. Recent polls show him at 38-41% in the first round on October 4, ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro at 33-37%, with both advancing to a runoff that polls rate as a statistical tie or narrow Lula advantage. The official campaign period began August 16, featuring debates and free broadcast time, while Jair Bolsonaro’s ongoing legal restrictions have consolidated right-wing support behind his son Flávio. Lower-polling candidates such as Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, and Renan Santos remain in single digits, limiting vote splitting on the right. Lula’s approval hovers near 47% amid mixed economic signals, contributing to the current pricing.

markets.description:

The primary resolution source will be official information from MLB (https://www.mlb.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: The tight contest between Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and J.D. Vance at near-even odds reflects trader assessments of their distinct bases within the Republican coalition ahead of the 2028 nomination. Vance benefits from his current role and alignment with core party priorities on trade, immigration enforcement, and institutional reform, while Kennedy draws support through crossover appeal on regulatory and health policy issues. Recent national and early-state polling shows both candidates maintaining steady but non-dominant shares among likely primary voters, with limited movement from endorsements or congressional actions. Rubio trails as a more conventional alternative, and the broader field remains fragmented. Key upcoming catalysts include midterm election results, confirmation votes, and any shifts in candidate positioning on foreign policy or fiscal matters that could consolidate support or prompt withdrawals.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2026 MLB World Series. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2026 MLB World Series per the rules of MLB (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 MLB season is cancelled, postponed after December 31, 2026 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from MLB (https://www.mlb.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Los Angeles Dodgers hold the top implied probability at 31% thanks to their deep roster, strong NL West standing near 81-54, and historical postseason experience despite pitching uncertainties around Shohei Ohtani. The Milwaukee Brewers sit at 12% on the strength of the majors' best record (84-51) and dominant NL Central form. The New York Yankees (9.5%) and Tampa Bay Rays (7%) benefit from AL East contention, with the Rays at 80-54. Other contenders like the Atlanta Braves, Philadelphia Phillies, and Chicago Cubs reflect solid division or wild-card positioning and recent momentum, while lower probabilities for teams such as the Houston Astros and San Diego Padres align with middling records and tougher paths through expanded playoffs. Late-August injury reports and divisional races continue to shape trader consensus.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2027 NFL league championship. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2027 NFL league championship per the rules of the NFL (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2027 NFL league championship game is cancelled, postponed after March 31, 2027 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from NFL (https://www.nfl.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This positions them ahead of a tightly bunched group where the Buffalo Bills, defending champion Seattle Seahawks, Baltimore Ravens, and others sit between roughly 4% and 9%. normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the 2026 Alaska gubernatorial election currently scheduled for November 3, 2026.  

If the results of the election are not confirmed by July 31, 2027, this market will resolve to "Other".  

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in Alaska for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on official certification.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins leads the Polymarket market at 48.1% following Tom Begich’s August 28–29 withdrawal and endorsement, which consolidates Democratic support ahead of the November 3 general election.** 

Begich had finished second in the August 18 top-four primary with roughly 21%, behind Kreiss-Tomkins at about 22%, while Republicans Bernadette Wilson (around 10%) and David Bronson (around 8%) advanced alongside them; the remaining field of 13 candidates split the rest of the vote. The open race, created by term-limited Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy, featured a crowded nonpartisan blanket primary with 17 candidates. Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state representative, benefits from unified Democratic and independent backing plus stronger fundraising, while Wilson, a conservative businesswoman and radio personality, leads the Republican side on issues like the Permanent Fund Dividend and fiscal restraint. Bronson, the former Anchorage mayor, trails as the other Republican qualifier. The ranked-choice general election and potential for further consolidation or late developments remain key variables shaping trader assessments of the outcome.

additional_prohibitions: Holders of federal and statewide public office.
Paid campaign staffers on Presidential campaigns.
Anyone working in a vote-tallying capacity, or who has the potential ability to observe official vote counts before they are public.
Third-party vendors and contractors (and employees thereof) of Presidential campaigns.
Paid employees of Democratic and Republican Party organizations, such as the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee or the Republican National Committee.
Paid employees of Political Action Committees (PACs) and “Super PACs” (independent expenditure only political committees).

Paid employees of major polling organizations. This prohibition does not apply to all employees of an organization that contains a polling division (e.g. the prohibition does not apply to all employees of Quinnipiac University despite the presence of Quinnipiac University’s polling division). The Exchange shall determine which polling organizations constitute “major” and may modify that determination at any time, and will post publicly a list of those organizations on its website

Employees of Decision Desks at major media organizations (including, but not necessarily exclusive to, Fox News, ABC News, AP, CNN, CBS News, Decision Desk HQ and NBC News). The Exchange shall determine which media organizations constitute “major” and may modify that determination at any time, and will post publicly a list of those organizations on its website.
All Electors who may cast ballots in connection with the determination of the President and/or Vice-President of the United States
All staff of the U.S. House of Representatives and its members
All staff of the U.S. Senate and its members.
All staff of the Office of the President of the United States
All staff of the Office of the Vice President of the United States
All staff of the U.S. Supreme Court and its Justices
Persons who are employed by any of the Source Agencies are not permitted to trade on the Contract.
Persons who hold any material, non-public information on the Underlying are not permitted to trade on the Contract.
Any candidate currently listed as a market within this event

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve to the player who wins the 2026 National League Most Valuable Player Award.

In the event of a tie, this market will resolve according to the official winner as determined by MLB rules. If multiple winners are announced then this market will resolve to the player whose listed last name comes first alphabetically.

If the 2026 MLB season is cancelled, postponed after December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Major League Baseball; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Pete Crow-Armstrong has established dominant trader consensus at 86.3% for 2026 NL MVP by leading MLB in fWAR (8.6) and bWAR (7.9) through elite center-field defense (23 outs above average), a 30-30 season with 33 home runs and 32 steals, plus top NL marks in slugging and wRC+. His resurgence at the plate combined with consistent baserunning and clutch production has widened the gap over Shohei Ohtani, whose left knee injury has limited him to DH duties since early July and stalled further pitching contributions after an 8-2 start with a 1.79 ERA. Expert polls reflect this shift, with most favoring Crow-Armstrong. Ohtani’s potential return to the mound or a late PCA slump could still narrow the implied probability margin before season’s end.

normalized_rules.rules_secondary:

normalized_rules.description:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gadi Eisenkot leads trader expectations for Israel's next prime minister following the October 27, 2026 Knesset election, reflecting his Yashar party's consistent polling gains over Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud amid voter fatigue with the incumbent's security record after the October 2023 Hamas attack and subsequent conflicts. Recent surveys show Eisenkot's party often edging or tying Likud in projected seats while he leads as preferred prime minister, aided by his former IDF chief of staff background and broad appeal across centrist and right-leaning voters. Netanyahu retains core support but contends with coalition bloc shortfalls below 61 seats in most forecasts, prompting discussions of potential unity arrangements. Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman trail as secondary options in fragmented opposition scenarios. These dynamics align with current market pricing as traders weigh coalition formation prospects in Israel's proportional representation system.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2026 MLB World Series. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2026 MLB World Series per the rules of MLB (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 MLB season is cancelled, postponed after December 31, 2026 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from MLB (https://www.mlb.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Los Angeles Dodgers hold the top implied probability at 31% thanks to their deep roster, strong NL West standing near 81-54, and historical postseason experience despite pitching uncertainties around Shohei Ohtani. The Milwaukee Brewers sit at 12% on the strength of the majors' best record (84-51) and dominant NL Central form. The New York Yankees (9.5%) and Tampa Bay Rays (7%) benefit from AL East contention, with the Rays at 80-54. Other contenders like the Atlanta Braves, Philadelphia Phillies, and Chicago Cubs reflect solid division or wild-card positioning and recent momentum, while lower probabilities for teams such as the Houston Astros and San Diego Padres align with middling records and tougher paths through expanded playoffs. Late-August injury reports and divisional races continue to shape trader consensus.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2027 NFL league championship. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2027 NFL league championship per the rules of the NFL (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2027 NFL league championship game is cancelled, postponed after March 31, 2027 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from NFL (https://www.nfl.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

series.title: House winner

resolution_criteria:
If the Democratic Party has won control of the House in 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
This market may be determined early based on a consensus of media calls projecting control of the U.S. House. See full rules for details. Otherwise, victory will be determined by the party identification of the Speaker of the House on February 1, 2027.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Democratic polling leads on the generic congressional ballot, averaging around D+6 in recent surveys, combined with President Trump's approval rating near 38%, form the core driver behind trader consensus heavily favoring Democratic House control in 2026. This environment aligns with historical midterm patterns where the president's party often faces headwinds, and recent race rating updates from forecasters have shifted additional Republican-held districts toward Democrats. Mid-decade redistricting provided some structural gains for Republicans in targeted states, yet forecasts project Democratic seat gains sufficient for a majority in most simulations. With roughly two months until Election Day, these fundamentals continue to shape assessments of the narrow current GOP majority.

Mid-decade redistricting provided some structural gains for Republicans in targeted states, yet forecasts project Democratic seat gains sufficient for a majority in most simulations. With roughly two months until Election Day, these fundamentals continue to shape assessments of the narrow current GOP majority.

events.title: Which party will win the House in 2026?

selected_market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?

resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

normalized_rules.description:
This market will resolve according to the team that wins the 2027 NFL league championship. 

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to win the 2027 NFL league championship per the rules of the NFL (e.g., they are eliminated in the playoffs), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2027 NFL league championship game is cancelled, postponed after March 31, 2027 ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from NFL (https://www.nfl.com/); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Los Angeles Rams hold the clearest edge in the 2027 champion market after aggressive offseason additions, including the acquisition of reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and cornerback Trent McDuffie, built on a roster that reached the NFC Championship last season behind Matthew Stafford’s MVP campaign and weapons like Puka Nacua. This positions them ahead of a tightly bunched group where the Buffalo Bills, defending champion Seattle Seahawks, Baltimore Ravens, and others sit between roughly 4% and 9%. The compressed probabilities reflect broad NFL parity, with multiple clubs featuring established quarterbacks, recent playoff experience, and solid depth, while roster turnover for the Seahawks and the absence of any overwhelming favorite keep outcomes competitive heading into the 2026 season.
